preamble: The voiced velar stop [ɡ] became the voiceless unaspirated palatal stop [c] in Lhasa Tibetan, combining palatalization with loss of voicing. The written clusters with a g- base and -y- medial (Old Tibetan *ɡʲ) preceded by the prefixes b- or s- are pronounced [c] with low tone: brgya 'hundred' is /ca˩˨/ and brgyad 'eight' is /cɛː˩˧˨/. The velar was palatalized by the medial -y-, the prefix was lost and the old voiced stop devoiced as part of Lhasa tonogenesis; with the prefix r- the outcome is often still voiced [ɟ] (rgyal po 'king' /ɟɛː˩˨.poˑ/). Icelandic g [c] before front vowels is the palatal allophone of the lenis /k/ and is filed under k > c.

examples.from: brgyud 'to pass through, be transmitted', Old Tibetan /*brɡʲut/

examples.note: The source sound is orthographic g followed by the medial y, reconstructed as palatalized *ɡʲ; Amdo dialects keep a voiced palatal (Zêkog /wɟja/ 'hundred').
